name: Starter: Urdu
about: Urdu word order, its little words after the noun and its agreement in real, everyday sentences, every word with the vowel marks a beginner needs until it is known.

words.میں: I (مَیں; مُجھے: to me); in (میں), after a place
words.ہونا: to be (ہوں: am; ہے: is; ہیں: are or respectful is; تھا: was)
words.کا: of, 's (کا, کی, کے agree with the linked noun or understood thing)
words.کتنا: how much (کِتنے کی: for how much)
words.چاہیے: is needed, should (مُجھے چاہِیے: I need)
words.کرنا: to do, make (کام کَرنا: to work)
words.کیسا: how; what kind (کَیسے ہیں: how are you)
words.گا: will (گا, گی, گے, after the verb)
words.نے: marks the doer with many completed transitive verbs
words.کو: to; on a day or time; marks some animate or specific objects

barah-karam.about: Literally by way of kindness; a polite request starts with it.

maaf-kijiye.about: Literally please forgive; to get someone's attention or say sorry.

concept.line: ہوں goes with مَیں, ہو with تُم, ہے with a singular subject, and ہیں with a plural subject or one respected person; they normally come last: مَیں طالِبِ عِلم ہوں; تُم کَیسے ہو؟; مَوسَم ٹَھنڈا ہے; اَبُّو اِنجِینِئَر ہیں.
A yes/no question can start with کیا and keeps a statement's order (کیا آپ اَنگریزی بولتے ہیں؟); a question word sits where its answer would: آپ کہاں رَہتے ہیں؟

words.means: میری = my; میرے = my; میرا = my

concept.line: میرا (my), ہَمارا (our) and آپ کا (your) come first and agree with what's owned, like کا: میرا بھائی, میری بَہَن, میرے دوست.
Urdu has no separate words for a, an or the; context supplies them: مَیں طالِبِ عِلم ہوں (I'm a student); میز پَر کِتابیں ہیں.

words.means: is needed; is wanted; should (after an infinitive)

concept.line: An Urdu sentence usually ends with its verb, with the object before it: مَیں چائے پِیتا ہوں (I drink tea); کَل مَیں بَس سے کام پَر جاؤں گا.

words.means: رہتا = live; رہتے = live; رہتی = lives
جاتا = go; جا = going; جاتی = goes

concept.line: The -تا, -تی or -تے form with ہوں, ہو, ہے or ہیں describes habits, repeated actions and general states: مَیں چائے پِیتا ہوں; اَمّی ہَسپَتال میں کام کَرتی ہیں.
